title: Joseph Smith: Rough Stone Rolling
author: Richard Lyman Bushman
target_audience: Scholars and students of American religious and 19th-century history
Members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (LDS Church)
General readers interested in biography and religious leaders
core_themes: The complexity and contradictions of Joseph Smith’s character
The historical context of early Mormonism in America
primary_purpose: To deliver an extensively researched, balanced, and nuanced biography of Joseph Smith, exploring his life, motivations, and the cultural context of his rise as the founder of Mormonism, while critically examining both his achievements and controversies.

structure_format.narrative_style: Scholarly yet accessible, intertwining narrative biography with historical analysis
structure_format.organization: Chronological, beginning with Smith’s ancestry and early life, moving through the founding of the LDS Church, revelations, social challenges, migrations, and ending with his death at Carthage Jail
features: Use of primary documents and sources
Contextualization within broader American religious movements

key_concepts_lessons: Joseph Smith was a product of a vibrant, tumultuous religious era in early America.
Smith’s claims of visions and revelations were both sincere and controversial, shaping a new religious tradition.
The formation and survival of Mormonism required considerable charisma, adaptability, and organizational skill.
Personal weaknesses and controversial doctrines (such as polygamy) contributed to external resistance and internal conflict.
Spiritual leaders can be both inspired and flawed, with an ongoing legacy shaped by their complexity.
notable_features: Written by a practicing Mormon and respected historian, offering both insider and scholarly perspectives
Examines both faith-promoting and challenging aspects of Smith’s life
Relies heavily on primary sources and contextual scholarship
Addresses controversial topics—polygamy, treasure-seeking, and the translation of scripture—directly
cultural_historical_context: Published amid increasing scholarly and public interest in the roots and expansion of Mormonism, as well as a period of greater openness in Mormon historical studies. The book contributed to more transparent academic discourse surrounding LDS history in the early 21st century.
reception_impact: Lauded for its thoroughness, fairness, and depth by both academic and religious communities
Helped shift Mormon historiography toward greater transparency and complexity
Cited as a model biography of a religious leader, with Bushman praised for balancing empathy with critical distance
Sparked ongoing discussions about the intersection of faith, scholarship, and historical truth among LDS audiences
comparable_titles: No Man Knows My History: The Life of Joseph Smith by Fawn M. Brodie
American Crucifixion: The Murder of Joseph Smith and the Fate of the Mormon Church by Alex Beam
Brigham Young: Pioneer Prophet by John G. Turner
